Dated this the 10th day of October, 2024 This Criminal Revision Petition has been filed under Sections 438 and 442 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, and the revision petitioner,
who is the sole accused in Crime No.1787/2016 of Aluva East Police Station, impugns order in CMP No.344/2024 in S.C.No.53/2019, whereby the learned Special Judge dismissed an application filed by the petitioner under Section 227 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.
2. Heard the learned counsel for the revision petitioner and the learned Public Prosecutor in detail.
Perused the relevant documents.

3. The prosecution case, as extracted in the order dated 03.10.2024 in CMP No.344/2024, is that the accused, with the intention of committing rape on the survivor and with the intention for making unlawful gain to him, had 2024:KER:76871 CRL.REV.PET NO. 1077 OF 2024 made the survivor believe that the soul of her deceased husband is embedded in the body of the accused and that the soul wanted to have sexual intercourse with the survivor.
Further the accused and the survivor were husband and wife during their previous birth and that they would remain as husband and wife in their future life also.
After making her to believe so, the accused had committed rape on the survivor on multiple occasions by making her believe that it was the soul of her erstwhile husband doing the sexual act.
That apart, he had appropriated the gold ornaments owned by the survivor from her and utilised the same for his own purposes.

The accused also had made her to avail loans from various financial institutions and appropriated the money for his purposes that the immovable property belonging to her had been pledged by him as security for encashing a chitty transaction which he had with the KSFE.
Further the accused had criminally intimidated her by threatening to kill her and 2024:KER:76871 CRL.REV.PET NO. 1077 OF 2024 her children if the matter was revealed to anybody.

Thereby the accused committed offences punishbale under Sections 376(2)(n), 406, 420, 506(ii) of IPC.
4.

The petitioner herein filed a petition seeking discharge, raising contention that no materials prima facie available to frame charge against the accused, and no ingredients of the offences of cheating, criminal breach, or rape are made out.
The prosecution side opposed the same.

The learned Special Judge addressed the contention at length and finally found that even a strong suspicion is sufficient in the ordinary course for framing charge against the accused and on consideration of the prosecution records, the offences are made out prima facie warranting trial.
5. While assailing the order, the learned counsel for the petitioner re-iterated the contention raised before the trial court.

The main contention raised are as summarised in paragraph Nos. 6, 7, and 9 and the same are 2024:KER:76871 CRL.REV.PET NO. 1077 OF 2024 as under:
"6.

There are several statements recorded during investigation which show that the ornaments which belonged to the survivor had been appropriated by the petitioner and that the ornaments Ramachandran vs State Of Kerala on 10 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39897458/

sentences.text: Therefore the defence contention that there is no evidence of entrustment of any property belonging to the survivor does not seem to be correct.

Whether there was any understanding between the survivor and the accused with regard to the manner in which the entrustment gold ornaments were to be dealt with by the petitioner is a matter that can be decided only after recording of evidence.
Therefore there is sufficient material for framing a charge against the accused, with regard to the offence of criminal breach of trust.

7. There are documents and statements recorded during investigation which will go to show that the petitioner had come in possession of the title deeds of immoveable property owned by the survivor and there is evidence to show that various loans were taken by the survivor herself as well as in the name of her son.
The prosecution contention is that the loan amounts had been appropriated by the petitioner.
What was the basis on which amounts were handed over to the petitioner is a matter that has to be 2024:KER:76871 CRL.REV.PET NO. 1077 OF 2024 decided after recording of evidence.

Going by the records so far collected and produced before court, it is seen that the properties of the survivor had been pledged and loans have been availed by the survivor and that the beneficiary of such pledges and loans have been the petitioner.

When there is obviously no relationship between the petitioner and the survivor's family which would compel the survivor and her son to incur financial liabilities for the benefit of the petitioner, it can be naturally inferred that the petitioner had come in possession of the money and assets of the survivor on the basis of some inducement which was made to her by the petitioner.
The contention of the petitioner that there was no inducement from his part which resulted in delivery of any property does not seem to be correct in these circumstances.

There is evidence collected by the investigating officer to show that the survivor in this case had incurred financial liabilities by way of loans and pledges in her name as well as in the name of her son.
8. xxxx 9.

Coming to the question of criminal intimation, there is a specific statement from the part of the survivor that even though she had understood that the petitioner had bene making misrepresentations to her and that she was sustaining financial loss as a result 2024:

CRL.REV.PET NO. 1077 OF 2024 of the actions done by her at the behest of the petitioner she did not reveal any of these aspects to any of her relatives for the reasons that the petitioner had criminally intimidated her by threatening that he would kill her and her children if the matters were revealed to anybody.
Such a circumstance is sufficient in the ordinary course of things to cause alarm to person who hears such a statement.

Therefore, it cannot be found that there is no evidence to attract the offence of criminal intimidation from the facts of the case."
6.
The learned Public Prosecutor opposed the contention by relying the prosecution records and pointing out the genesis of the prosecution case under misconception of fact, which would vitiate consent.

7. Going through the prosecution records and the statements of the witnesses at part with the allegations, it is discernible that the accused, with the intention of committing rape on the survivor and with the intention for making unlawful gain to him, had made the survivor believe Ramachandran vs State Of Kerala on 10 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39897458/
3 2024:KER:76871 CRL.REV.PET NO. 1077 OF 2024 that the soul of her deceased husband is embedded in the body of the accused and that the soul wanted to have sexual intercourse with the survivor.
Further the accused and the survivor were husband and wife during their previous birth and that they would remain as husband and wife in their future life also.
After making her to believe so, the accused had committed rape on the survivor on multiple occasions by making her believe that it was the soul of her erstwhile husband doing the sexual act.
That apart, he had appropriated the gold ornaments owned by the survivor from her and utilised the same for his own purposes.

The accused also had made her to avail loans from various financial institutions and appropriated the money for his purposes that the immovable property belonging to her had been pledged by him as security for encashing a chitty transaction which he had with the KSFE.
Further the accused had criminally intimidated her by threatening to kill her and her children if 2024:KER:76871 CRL.REV.PET NO. 1077 OF 2024 the matter was revealed to anybody.
Therefore, there is no reason to hold that finding of the trial court in the discharge petition is erroneous so as to have interference.
That apart, the prosecution materials prima facie show materials warranting trial of this case.

8. In this connection, it is relevant to note that as per Section 90 of the IPC, a consent is not such a consent as is intended by any section of the Indian Penal Code, if the consent is given by a person under fear of injury, or under a misconception of fact, and if the person doing the act knows, or has reason to believe, that the consent was given in consequence of such fear or misconception.

Section 90 of IPC reads as under:
"90. Consent known to be given under fear or misconception.--

A consent is not such a consent as it intended by any section of this Code, if the consent is given by a person under fear of injury, or under a misconception of fact,
and if the person doing the act 2024:KER:76871 CRL.REV.PET NO. 1077 OF 2024 knows, or has reason to believe, that the consent was given in consequence of such fear or misconception; or Consent of insane person.-- if the consent is given by a person who, from unsoundness of mind, or intoxication, is unable to understand the nature and consequence of that to which he gives his consent; or Consent of child.--
unless the contrary appears from the context, if the consent is given by a person who is under twelve years of age."
9. Thus consent is vitiated when the same is obtained by misconception of fact.

In the instant case,
the prosecution alleges that the petitioner dominated the will of the defacto complainant, making her to believe that the depicted soul of her husband embedded in the body of the accused and on the said misconception, he had obtained consent to have coitus with the defacto complainant and continued the same.
The prosecution records do justify the same prima facie.
Therefore, whether the relation is purely consensual or the consent is vitiated by misconception of fact in the facts discussed herein above is a matter of evidence.
Therefore, the petitioner can raise his contention during trial in a case where charge already 2024:KER:76871 CRL.REV.PET NO. 1077 OF 2024 framed.
Hence, this petition fails and is dismissed accordingly.
